result_text:
`Tool.from_function(fn)` and `FunctionTool.from_function(fn)` now use the `@tool` decorator's metadata when the caller passes no `metadata=` and no individual metadata keyword arguments. I ran your `greet` example with all the decorator fields, and the tool comes out with name `custom-greet`, version `v1`, the given title, description `Greets` and the given tags and meta.

The change is in `FunctionTool.from_function` in `src/fastmcp/tools/function_tool.py`, which looks up the function's `ToolMeta` and uses it. `Tool.from_function` just calls that method, so it needed no edit. The `ToolMeta` is used whole, so the other stored fields (icons, annotations, output schema, task, timeout, auth and so on) apply too.

An explicit `metadata=` or any individual keyword still takes effect as before, with no merging. Passing both still raises the same `TypeError`. Functions with no decorator metadata, or with a non-`ToolMeta` `__fastmcp__`, behave as before.

The `tests/tools` suite passes (306 passed, 1 skipped) and ruff is clean on `src/fastmcp/tools`. I didn't add a dedicated test for the new behaviour. I also didn't run the full suite or the `prek` hooks, and an earlier combined run of `tests/tools` and `tests/server` never reported its pytest result (only the script output and ruff came back).
